title: Hang a weighted tube level on a single conveyor hook
instruction: Hang the tube level on the hook.
context: On powder-coating and paint lines, long parts are hung from single hooks on an overhead conveyor and must hang level so the coating runs evenly and the part clears the line; a single-point lift needs the same. A steel slug sealed inside this tube puts its balance point 6 to 14 cm from the middle (it changes with the trial seed), and the hook's cradle is only 4 cm wide. Nothing outside shows the slug: the robot must find the balance point by test lifts (lift, see which end drops, move the grip toward it), then hang the tube on the hook at that point and let go. Once lifted clear, the tube must not touch the table again.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table top (x forward, y left, z up). Arms start in the ready pose. Tube: sealed 6061 aluminium tube, 50 mm outside diameter, 1.5 mm wall, 100 cm long, lying on the table along y with its middle at x 18, y -8; press-fit PE end plugs 3 cm long, red at the left (+y) end and blue at the right (-y) end; inside, a 40 mm diameter, 35 mm long steel slug (345 g) glued at a seeded position (README table); total mass 1.01 kg. Hook station (fixed, clamped to the table), standing in for one hanging point of an overhead conveyor: steel base plate 12 x 12 x 1.2 cm and 3 x 3 cm post at x 48, y -5; a 2 x 2 cm steel arm from the post's top toward the arms, 22 to 24 cm above the table; from its end a 10 mm steel J-hook hangs down to a cradle centred at x 33, y -5, 4 cm wide along y, rubber-lined, opening toward the arms; its 90-degree rubber V seat has its upper edges 10.3 cm above the table (the front edge is the lip) and touches a 50 mm tube 9.2 cm above the table; a tube hanging in it has its axis 11.0 cm above the table. Nothing else on the table. Tape the tube's start outline.
scoring: Latched over the whole trial: 0 if, after the tube was lifted clear (lowest point 5 cm or more above the table, or carried by the hook alone), it touches the table or floor again, or if it is dropped (falls 2 cm with nothing touching it). Otherwise: 1.0 (success) when the tube hangs in the hook's cradle (axis within 1.5 cm sideways and 1 cm in height of the seated position, 11.0 cm above the table, nothing else touching it), level within 3 degrees, still, with both grippers at least 80% open, every finger pad 5 cm or more from the tube and no robot contact, held for 2 s; 0.75 for the same state not yet held 2 s at the end; 0.5 on the hook and level but held, touched or moving; 0.25 lifted clear but not on the hook; else 0. Level is checked with an inclinometer, the 5 cm gaps and contacts from the video.
reset_notes: Take the tube off the hook and lay it back in its taped outline, red plug to the left. To change the seed, move the slug: it sits 2.93 times the balance-point offset from the middle (README table); glue it with a dab of epoxy or fix it with a set screw.
fidelity: Approximate. The tube is one PhysX rigid body (cylinder collider, friction 0.8); the slug sets its centre of mass and inertia (written with PhysX's tensor API at every reset) and has no geometry. The hook station is a kinematic body of boxes and the hook is rigid (a real conveyor hook swings a little); its V seat is two 45-degree rubber plates. The gripped tube tilts through the arm's compliance and slip between the pads. Table contact is geometric (lowest point within 2 mm of the table); hook and robot contacts are PhysX contact forces. Details in README.
